laws.law: Streaming circuit breakers need silence-based detection, distribution-derived deadlines, and background probes.
laws.incident: An 8s deadline inside the primary's ordinary tail made the fallback write half of all output.

laws.law: Treat deploys and edge timeouts as first-class failure sources for long requests.
laws.incident: 23 deploys in 17 hours cut 68 streams.

laws.law: Measure under concurrency and never memoize a failed read.
laws.incident: Eight queries at 1–2s each crossed the timeout together.

laws.law: “Done” includes the thing that invokes it: schedule, prompt, caller, proven not assumed.
laws.incident: The billing-anomaly alert never executed once.

laws.law: Choose failure direction per asymmetry of harm, explicitly, per gate.
laws.incident: A billing gate's unknown state must not grant anything.

laws.law: Money bugs surface at a fraction of their blast radius; audit the ledger, not the inbox.
laws.incident: Only 1 of 3 double-charged users complained.

laws.law: Every automated touch needs a success event or it does not ship live.
laws.incident: One message sent 2,547 times with zero successes.

laws.law: Ship dark, activate separately, and make rollback a one-line config change.
laws.incident: An auto-starting flow took 84 minutes to revert.

laws.law: Define activation as a small count of real actions in session one and optimize the minutes after signup.
laws.incident: Setup completed 95%; 38% of completers never did anything.

laws.law: Generate first from inferred defaults; make questions the retention loop, not the entry fee.
laws.incident: A “first win” flow started from nothing completed 3.4%; from an existing draft, 47%.

laws.law: All guidance surfaces derive from a single source of truth so they cannot drift into two voices.
laws.incident: “In an effort for simplicity we made this more complicated.”

laws.law: Interface parity is an audit with file-and-line gaps; an assisted action carries its result and its link back, and never claims a write it did not make.
laws.incident: “I'll open it now” was structurally unkeepable.

laws.law: If any assistant or support bot answers from your documentation, that documentation is a build artifact gated in CI, written before the change.
laws.incident: “If behavior changes and the manual doesn't, the assistant starts lying.”

laws.law: Treat every UI claim as a factual assertion with a source; when the source is missing, render nothing.
laws.incident: A preview invented a dollar figure.

laws.law: Prices and claims are data, deduplicated and tested like code.
laws.incident: Stale pricing survived two price changes.

laws.law: Social proof is computed, curated, and cannot show a complaint or an insider.
laws.incident: A test account appeared in the “just upgraded” widget.

laws.law: Ask after value, from people in a good mood, with the same offer for all, and never by email.
laws.incident: 45% of day-zero claimers upgraded zero.

laws.law: Verify crawlability end to end from outside with the bot's own identity, and treat auth middleware as part of SEO.
laws.incident: Every AI crawler was blocked at the edge; 5 of 11 public routes redirected crawlers to login.

laws.law: Lifecycle mail is judged by what the recipient did next, and it must hand them something to do.
laws.incident: Post-send activity after a draft-hook email was 41–45% (uncontrolled); on the strict click-then-return read the best message managed 10 of 436 and every paid pitch 0 of 274.

laws.law: All outbound messaging shares one idempotent ledger that caps and analytics read.
laws.incident: A broadcast outside the ledger silenced the caps the next day.

laws.law: Usage limits convert when they interrupt real value; measure activation by self-initiated use, never by hitting the limit.
laws.incident: An auto-generated first result manufactured cap hits without payers.

laws.law: Never make stopping payment harder than starting it.
laws.incident: Cancel clicked five times on a greyed-out button.

laws.law: Automated outreach exists only inside a conversation the customer opened, is short and warm, and can be stopped without a deploy.
laws.incident: An unprompted message reached someone who had written to nobody.

laws.law: Anything the customer must be able to predict is code, with the model as fallback for the remainder.
laws.incident: A preference stored twice and injected every turn was still ignored.

laws.law: Heuristics are measured on real traffic with pinned false positives, never tuned by intuition.
laws.incident: A word the rule read as a request for an image meant a story in 961 real messages.

laws.law: Any change to a probabilistic component (model, ranking, search, recommendation, vendor) is an experiment with controls, blinding, cost accounting and a shadow phase.
laws.incident: A judge that prefers “A” whichever side A is on measures position.

laws.law: Multi-agent development needs isolation, explicit ownership, and verification of what is actually running.
laws.incident: Auto-merge sat dead a week on stale code.

cadence.name: Silent-failure canaries
items: Health check on yesterday's complete local day: broken-output share, with a decision table and a report even when quiet.
Fallback or degraded share of output; alert above a threshold.
Grounding or retrieval rate against a healthy band.
Money ledger reconcile against the processor, deduped by fingerprint.
Stranded work in any queue a human is supposed to see.

cadence.name: The Monday scoreboard
items: Day-zero depth, week-one return, engaged weekly actives, day-one return, per tenure, in the named timezone, against dated targets.
Paid adds this week and the ceiling they imply.
Every negative rating and complaint from the week, root-caused.
Ads by cost per activated user, joined from production.

cadence.name: Per-surface audits
items: One funnel end to end, by identity, with the leak named and the blocked reasons beside it.
The email program: click-then-return per message, holdout deltas, zero-signal rows to cut.
What users are not using: every element ranked by reach × second-day return.
Every public claim and every help sentence against the code.
A corpus replay of any classifier or routing rule touched since last time.

cadence.name: Models and money
items: Backtest the revenue projection against actuals; replace the weakest assumption with a measured interval.
Re-measure churn on exposure; check the resubscriber and comp conventions.
Review funnel with batch minutes filtered; listing ratings refreshed.
Crawler access from outside with each bot's user agent.
A bake-off for any vendor or algorithm swap; never a swap without a shadow phase.

cadence.name: The gates
items: Blast radius counted in production before the fix.
Adversarial review with an independent refuter per finding; fewer than two verdicts is unreviewed.
Help and public copy updated first; CI fails otherwise.
Ship dark behind a flag; a decision day is a config flip.
End-to-end check as a real user on production data before saying done.

audit_kit.question: Is this rate falling, or is its denominator growing?
audit_kit.trap: “All users ever” in the denominator; a base that aged; today's partial bar.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Re-read per tenure and per cohort; act only on the residual.

audit_kit.question: Does the source actually say this, and did anything later overturn it?
audit_kit.trap: A number copied from a plan that was retracted by name.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Every headline claim gets a hostile second reader before it steers a budget.

audit_kit.question: Which automated touches have ≥50 exposures and 0 successes?
audit_kit.trap: Success events with unknown names that resolve to nothing; dead sends that look busy.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Kill, or give it a success event and re-seed inactive.

audit_kit.question: What is broken that nobody will report?
audit_kit.trap: HTTP 200 with empty output; a flag that self-erases; an alert nobody scheduled.
audit_kit.decision_rule: A field written unconditionally, scored on one complete day, reported daily.

audit_kit.question: Does our record of money agree with the processor's?
audit_kit.trap: Webhooks lost, redelivered or repointed; one event family filtered out.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Count by transaction, both families, nightly; assume silent victims.

audit_kit.question: What does this rule do to every real message ever sent?
audit_kit.trap: A regex tuned by intuition; a verifier that silently died.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Before/after counts, hand-read matches, pinned regressions; ambiguous → null.

audit_kit.question: Which sentences in the product are false right now?
audit_kit.trap: A trial that was removed; a badge over the wrong data; help describing the old UI.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Machine-check every quoted string, number and path; pin each wrong sentence as a guard.

audit_kit.question: Where does one person's journey actually end?
audit_kit.trap: Percent of the top; mixing instruments; events an ad blocker hides.
audit_kit.decision_rule: One rank per person, rungs proven by durable truths, blocked reasons on the rung.

audit_kit.question: Has this cohort's window closed before we read it?
audit_kit.trap: Right-censoring; crediting pre-deploy sends with post-deploy successes.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Read on dated checkpoints; say what can and cannot be claimed at that n.

audit_kit.question: What did each ad cost per activated user and per payer?
audit_kit.trap: The platform's lead count; audience saturation blamed on creative.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Join by campaign tag; steer on activation and payback vs LTV.

audit_kit.question: How many organic reviews does the program actually produce?
audit_kit.trap: Backfill batches counted as claims; a gate that verifies nothing.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Filter batch minutes; instrument impressions; hedge routing.

audit_kit.question: What did the agent read, refuse, and send, and did two readings agree?
audit_kit.trap: A wording gate that releases 1 of 54; a rule that quietly empties the queue.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Evidence per lane; refusals recorded on the job; a kill switch that is a row.

audit_kit.question: What was the top cause of every negative rating and abandoned session this week?
audit_kit.trap: Blaming “quality” when the cause is a cap, a routing rule or spliced text; ratings that reach nobody.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Read every negative rating and transcript every 3–5 days; fix the top cause with a test; the reply is a consequence.

audit_kit.question: Who never used the product, when do activators act, what does email do, and where do guided flows die?
audit_kit.trap: Optimizing setup when the death point is the empty screen after it.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Never-used share, time to first request, email's share of first returns, guided-flow completion from nothing vs from a result.

audit_kit.question: Does every number on the board mean what its label says?
audit_kit.trap: An open rate that is a click rate; “active” that includes page loads; a day-offset mislabeled by one.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Re-derive each headline metric from raw rows; put two numerators over one denominator; fix the instrument before judging the product.

audit_kit.question: Where does intent to pay leak before the charge?
audit_kit.trap: A click that “does nothing” and is clicked again; a promised trial that no longer exists; a key one character too long.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Event funnel modal → click → form → card → paid with a loading state on every step; every promise in the flow checked against the plan constant.

audit_kit.question: Do the modules work and does the connective tissue between them?
audit_kit.trap: Excellent interiors stapled together by dead-end chrome, duplicate doors and decorative showcases.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Two personas, real screenshots, phone width; score interiors and hallways separately; fix the revenue-critical funnel bugs first.

audit_kit.question: Did signups per fresh visitor within seven days move?
audit_kit.trap: Judging a door by its leak; no pre-change era to compare against; internal browsers in the window.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Fresh visitors (bot-filtered, per browser), primary action, signup within 7 days; ≥1,000 fresh visitors per arm before a verdict.

audit_kit.question: Can each bot, by its own user agent, fetch every public route from outside?
audit_kit.trap: robots.txt read as evidence; a CDN rule above your own; public routes redirecting to login.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Fetch every public path as each crawler after any change; diff the sitemap against the auth allowlist.

audit_kit.question: Does the ad platform see the pages the campaigns point at, and do signups carry their source?
audit_kit.trap: No pixel on the landing the ads point at; attribution fields on an unused form; installs posing as a channel.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Mount points vs the route tree; a test signup per source; the unattributed share decomposed by month.

audit_kit.question: Is usage actually down, or is the chart?
audit_kit.trap: Today's partial bar drawn full; the weekday shape; deploys cutting streams.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Same weekday, same hour comparisons; drop today; correlate failures with deploy timestamps before touching the product.

audit_kit.question: Does the candidate beat a fresh baseline on real inputs?
audit_kit.trap: A judge that prefers whichever side is “A”; a cheaper option that fails less mistaken for one that works better.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Real inputs, blind judges in both orders, cost accounting, a shadow phase before any swap.

audit_kit.question: Did last month's forecast land, and which assumption failed?
audit_kit.trap: A compounding model; an assumed churn; a caveat that switches itself off below a threshold.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Compare projection to actuals on a dated schedule; replace the weakest assumption with a measured interval; quote the ceiling, not the far month.

audit_kit.question: What do users believe the product is?
audit_kit.trap: Building what you think it should be.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Typed intents vs example prompts, return timing, converting surface, support tickets by what they were, one churned user traced second by second; every two weeks.

audit_kit.question: Is the loop producing activated invitees, or impressions?
audit_kit.trap: Rewards paid on send; impressions counted as yield; a loop built before intake exists.
audit_kit.decision_rule: Invitations, qualifications and payouts as durable rows per week; kill or pause if intake is flat.

practices.practice: Behavioral event ledger with root-layout click capture
practices.what: Every page view and click with a stable anonymous id before signup, explicit events for modals, sends and subscriptions; a client queue that debounces and redacts; server-origin events kept separate from user activity.
practices.why: Attribution once lived only on an unused page; email sends once counted as daily activity.

practices.what: Every headline number is a versioned database function; new definitions ship as new function names, never edited in place.
practices.why: A whole event table was streamed into application code three times per cache miss; a 1,000-row API cap silently truncated totals.

practices.what: Day-zero depth, week-one return, engaged weekly actives, day-one return, per tenure, in the named timezone, against four- and ten-week targets; era-split tiles pinned to deploy times.
practices.why: Targets that exceeded the sum of the plan's own lever sizes were re-scoped only after a scoreboard made the gap visible.

practices.cadence: every 3–5 days; per rating once automated
practices.what: Every thumbs-down with a reason becomes a job that reconstructs the thread from events and messages and ships a fix with a test; the reply, if any, is a consequence.
practices.why: “Model quality” was never the cause; a token cap, a greedy routing rule and spliced refusal text were.

practices.practice: Adversarial review with refuters and tracers
practices.cadence: every plan, money change, large change
practices.what: Finders over named lenses → an independent refuter and a code-path tracer per finding → tiebreak → confirmed counts in the change record → the fix diff reviewed the same way. Fewer than two verdicts is unreviewed.
practices.why: Fixes reintroduced defects in three of four rounds; a review that lost its verifiers silently marked 48 findings refuted.

practices.practice: Corpus replay before any rule change
practices.what: Run the old and new rule over every real input ever received; report before/after counts; hand-read every changed match; pin the inputs that broke as regression tests.
practices.why: A word the rule read as an image request meant a story in 961 real messages.

practices.practice: Dated plans that open with the last plan's report card
practices.what: Each plan grades the prior deploy against production, retracts earlier numbers by name, sizes each lever to a range labeled grind vs jump, and schedules read dates (machinery check → click read → causal read).
practices.why: A “+7-point” lever was re-sized to +1–3 and read flat; without the report card the number would have been reused.

practices.what: Read-only queries scored on the previous complete day with a decision table, backtested thresholds, a content-based estimator independent of any flag, and a report every day including quiet ones.
practices.why: Ten days of 6% broken output produced zero tickets.

practices.practice: Silent-failure watch jobs posting to one thread
practices.what: Output-property canary (hourly), degraded share (daily), money reconcile (nightly), stranded drafts (three times a day), deduped by fingerprint so silence means clean.
practices.why: A retrieval outage ran four days at HTTP 200; three double charges drew one complaint.

practices.what: Every sender claims (user, message, instance, channel) before calling the provider; statuses sent / skipped / failed / holdout; the provider id is the webhook join key; broadcasts write rows too.
practices.why: Check-then-send produced 1.6–1.8× duplicates; a broadcast outside the ledger had no open rate and silenced the caps.

practices.practice: Behavior-triggered lifecycle engine with global send rules
practices.what: Messages stored as rows (trigger, filters, priority, success event); windows, caps, suppression on success or activity; every non-send is a named skip reason counted per run.
practices.why: A linear drip could not react to behavior and could not explain a non-send.

practices.what: Hashed 20% buckets per experiment; exposure is a ledger row invisible to caps; a program-level no-mail holdout for new users; analysis windows exclude pre-treated users.
practices.why: Every retention claim without a control arm was ~5× inflated.

practices.what: Bare run prints; one flag sends a single test copy; the send flag only on the founder's explicit word; paged reads compared to an exact count; the script refuses a partial audience.
practices.why: A campaign audience came out as 101 of 3,015 because of a silent row cap.

practices.practice: Flag-dark launches with config-flip kill switches
practices.what: Features merge off; a decision day is a config flip; the previous branch is one variable away; deploy cutovers are recorded in flags and epochs.
practices.why: An auto-starting flow took 84 minutes to revert when the revert needed a deploy.

practices.what: Each incident, audit and rule lands as a cross-linked note with the numbers, the trap, the query filter and the application rule, indexed for the next person or session.
practices.why: Without them the same 35-call hunt was about to be re-run.

practices.what: Each migration opens with the incident or measurement, the numbers, the ordering law, and what is deliberately not done; applied files are stamped and frozen.
practices.why: A redefinition that did not restate a security property took signups down 3.5 hours.

practices.what: Path-scoped workflows fail any product change unless the help text an assistant answers from changed in the same diff or the change declares why not; corrected claims become guard tests.
practices.why: Twelve wrong help claims, four telling free users to pay for what they had.

practices.what: Every support message, form and negative rating becomes a job; a fix lands in a throwaway branch; a hostile second read merges or holds; the deploy is verified against that report; only then does the reply go.
practices.why: A reply once said “fixed” 37 seconds after the fix was held.

practices.practice: Deny-by-default send gate with a database-row kill switch
practices.what: Forbidden rules per lane (our fault, money moving, promises, other customers, hedging, grovelling); refusals written on the job; the switch read fresh on every send, unreadable counts as off.
practices.why: A wording-based gate released 1 of 54 drafts and made the founder the support team.

practices.what: Only questions and reviews push to the founder's phone; replies and thumbs-ups route back into the same run; a typed instruction becomes queued work; notices never interrupt.
practices.why: An agent that found asking expensive guessed instead.

practices.practice: Production end-to-end checks as a real user
practices.what: Mint a session as a real user; drive production APIs or a local build under the production environment with every write stubbed; reusable scripts verify shipped behavior; before/after screenshots at phone width.
practices.why: A referral end-to-end check caught a 3.5-hour signup outage that monitoring missed.

practices.what: Tests read source to pin laws: SQL ↔ code ids, function properties, exact call-site counts, no hardcoded prices, exactly two broadcasters; safety rules asserted by feeding the exact bad input.
practices.why: A safety regex shipped with a backspace where a word boundary should have been and matched nothing for 30 days.

practices.what: Subjects as user-facing sentences; bodies open with the customer's or founder's verbatim words, reconstruct the session from events, carry the counts, the root cause, and what was deliberately not changed.
practices.why: Reviewers and future readers verify the change from the record instead of re-deriving it.

practices.what: Counts of affected rows and users precede every migration or behavior change; reconcile jobs run live against production before shipping.
practices.why: “Quantify the population before you change it.”

practices.what: Reporting floors at the minute instrumentation became complete; every staff address and any browser ever signed in internally is excluded; test loads self-mark with a query parameter; feedback is never floored.
practices.why: Six of ten “visitors” in the first clean window were the team.

practices.what: One row per identity at its furthest rung, each rung proven by a durable truth (auth email, request count, subscription id), blocked reasons on the rung where the journey ended.
practices.why: Percent-of-top funnels widened and ad blockers hid client events.

practices.practice: Ad reads by cost per activated user
practices.what: Every ad joined to production by campaign tag; ranked by cost per activated user and per payer vs gross LTV; re-derived by a skeptic; dated reads with kill rules per audience and placement.
practices.why: The platform's cost per lead sat flat while true cost quadrupled.

practices.what: Fetch every public path as each crawler after any change; purge the CDN first; any measurement taken while blocked is invalid.
practices.why: Every AI crawler was blocked at the edge for months while robots.txt said allowed.

practices.what: Counts and ratings render a committed value first and swap to a cached live read (user count every 5 minutes, listing rating every 6 hours); the read never throws; a stale exact number is the honest fallback.
practices.why: A hardcoded count and a rounded “+” both had to be removed.

practices.practice: Competitor teardown → gap matrix → waved plan
practices.what: Public docs, help centers, pricing and review sites read into a graded matrix (table stakes / important / differentiator), a “where we already lead, do not regress” list, explicit non-goals, waves sized in days.
practices.why: The one capability no competitor had became the headline.

practices.practice: Shadow mode and blind judging before a vendor swap
practices.what: A candidate answers a slice of real traffic in the background, never shown; two judges read every pair blind in both orders under a daily cost cap; go/no-go rules printed beside intervals.
practices.why: “Writes better” turned out to be “fails less often”.

practices.practice: Deterministic fast paths ahead of the model
practices.what: Parsers, price answers, intent routing, suggestion governors, formatting rewrites, edit guards: pure libraries with truth-table tests and a null fall-through to the model.
practices.why: A stored preference was ignored ten times; the rewrite held.

practices.practice: Exit-intent question instead of an offer
practices.what: “Was anything confusing?” fires once per browser after finished work, never on cursor-leave or idle; answers go to the team and appear verbatim above every chart.
practices.why: Someone on their way out has already declined the offer.

belief_signals.showed: Requests peaked in the two days before a recurring deadline at 2.2× the trough day. The job ran on a cycle.
belief_signals.changed: Rewards and asks anchored to the user's natural cycle, not to a daily streak.

belief_signals.showed: The most-typed topic was absent from every example prompt; the most prominent example ranked eleventh.
belief_signals.changed: Example prompts re-ranked from organic topics.

belief_signals.showed: One in five support tickets was someone trying to use the product through the support box. People believed the support bubble was the product.
belief_signals.changed: The launcher moved; a classifier routes prompts to the product and questions to a human.

belief_signals.showed: Only the usage limit converted; sidebar and header offers barely did; email pitches not at all.
belief_signals.changed: Paid pitches by email removed; the first limit hit became a clean single-CTA pitch.

belief_signals.showed: Users asked for the default behavior they already knew from mainstream tools in the category; visitors treated the product as the general version, not the specialized one.
belief_signals.changed: The expected default became a mode; the specialized pitch moved to after the first result. Read the comparison users make in their first sessions and ship that expectation as a mode before you fight it.

belief_signals.signal: Where they were sent vs where they meant to go
belief_signals.showed: Ads bought clicks to the paid suite and delivered the people to the free product for weeks; the audit called the two “stapled together”.
belief_signals.changed: If you sell more than one thing, each has its own door and the origin is recorded once at signup; verify the ad's landing → signup → destination path as a real user before spending.

belief_signals.showed: A meetings feature: 29 real uses in 90 days. A journal entry point: 28 users ever. Showcase cards drew 39 clicks against 289 on the sidebar across eight modules.
belief_signals.changed: The cut list; decorative showcases removed.

metrics.name: Instrumentation coverage
metrics.definition: Two shares from an event registry you maintain by hand: (a) user-facing surfaces with a registered impression event ÷ all surfaces that can convert; (b) money event names (checkout started, first paid, cancel, refund) with exactly one emitter ÷ all money event names. Internal-account and bot rules applied in every counter.
metrics.benchmark: 100% / 100% before the reporting epoch is reset. Reference: one preloaded form told 178 people they had started entering a card because one event name had two behaviors.
metrics.trap: A count of events firing is not coverage; count named surfaces and emitters from a registry, not from traffic.

metrics.name: Day-zero activation
metrics.definition: Share of new accounts that make ≥3 core requests AND keep/save one result on day zero (reporting-timezone day of signup). Denominator: signups on that day, internal accounts and bots excluded.
metrics.benchmark: 4.9% → 8.7% after generating the first result before any setup question (e-01, deploy)
metrics.trap: Never use 'reached the usage limit' as activation; an auto-generated first result manufactures it without payers.

metrics.name: First request within 1h / 24h
metrics.definition: Among accounts with ≥1 core request ever (requesters), the share whose first core request came within 60 minutes / within 24 hours of the signup timestamp (server clock); also report the median minutes. Exclude accounts younger than 24h.
metrics.benchmark: ~75% within 1h, 83% within 24h (b-time-to-first-request)
metrics.trap: Users stuck at 48h rarely come back to start; stop optimizing their emails, fix the first screen.

metrics.name: Setup completers with zero requests
metrics.definition: Among accounts ≥7 days old at read time: share that finished setup and never made a core request; also report the share of all registered accounts with zero requests.
metrics.benchmark: 38% of completers, 41% of all registered, measured with same-day signups included; expect a few points lower under this recipe (b-never-used-after-signing-up)
metrics.trap: Setup completion (95%) tells you nothing on its own.

metrics.name: Fill rate per setup field
metrics.definition: Per setup field: accounts that saved a non-default, non-empty value ÷ accounts that saw the field (impression event), trailing 30 days.
metrics.benchmark: one field filled by 1 of 1,445; another by 16.5%; setup then cut to two decisions (78 s, 96% complete)
metrics.trap: A prefilled default counts as unfilled; fill rate tells you what to delete, not whether onboarding works.

metrics.name: One-and-done share
metrics.definition: Among accounts ≥14 days old with ≥1 core request: share whose requests all fall on exactly one reporting-timezone day. Beside it: the top 5% of requesters by lifetime requests and their share of total volume.
metrics.benchmark: 55% one-and-done; 6% of requesters made 38% of volume; later 47% and 16% / 69% (b-one-and-done)
metrics.trap: Young accounts are one-and-done by construction; age-gate the denominator or the share rises with every signup burst.

metrics.name: Week-one return by day-zero depth
metrics.definition: Share of a signup cohort with ≥1 core request on reporting-timezone days 1–7, bucketed by core requests on day zero (0 / 1–2 / 3–5 / 6+). Same shape for pre-signup depth if you allow try-before-signup. Read only cohorts whose day 7 has closed.
metrics.benchmark: 0 requests 14% → 6+ requests 56% (strict definition); cold signup 26% vs 48% for visitors who used the whole free allowance (e-04, correlation); cohort blend ~32–33% (67% of new accounts never return in days 1–7)
metrics.trap: Correlational: users self-select. If depth rises and the cohort rate does not, the depth was manufactured.

metrics.name: Retention curve
metrics.definition: For signups in a 60-day cohort window: share with ≥1 core request on reporting-timezone day a after signup, a = 1,2,3,5,7,14,21,30,45; drop members whose day a has not fully elapsed; day zero is the denominator, never a column. Plot any-touch as a second numerator on the same denominator.
metrics.benchmark: any-touch: 26 / 18 / 14 / 11 / 12 / 11 / 11 / 9 / 9 (d1…d45); the request-based curve was not recorded in the source, expect lower (b-retention-curve)
metrics.trap: Any-touch retention counts page views; the request curve is the one to steer by.

metrics.name: Per-tenure engagement
metrics.definition: Share of accounts with a core request in the trailing 7 complete days, bucketed by account age (0–7d, 8–14d, 15–28d, 29–56d, 57+); the 0–7d bucket counts days 1–7 only (day zero excluded).
metrics.benchmark: week-one tenure 48.8% → 63.1% across the activation fixes; week 2 ~22%, then level
metrics.trap: Never steer by the blend over 'all users ever'; it falls mechanically as the base ages.

metrics.name: Daily / weekly actives by request
metrics.definition: Distinct non-internal accounts with ≥1 core request on a complete reporting-timezone day (DAU) or trailing 7 complete days (WAU); plot the any-touch numerator on the same axis; drop today.
metrics.benchmark: daily-active free users 183 → 282 between mid-July and late August (no pre-change arm, e-09); peak weekday 2.2× the trough
metrics.trap: Email sends and telemetry touches logged as activity produced two weeks of 90% 'DAU'; only a core request counts.

metrics.name: Paid conversion by pre-pay usage
metrics.definition: Share of accounts that ever paid, banded by core requests made BEFORE first paid (all requests for never-payers): ≤5, 6–19, 20–49, 50–99, 100+; accounts ≥30 days old.
metrics.benchmark: 0.6 / 5.3 / 19.8 / 42.4 / 78.3 (measured on lifetime usage, which flatters the top band); 69% of the base sat in the first band
metrics.trap: Banding by lifetime usage counts requests the payment unlocked; band on pre-pay usage. Separately: a base stuck in the first band is an activation problem, not a pricing problem.

metrics.name: Limit-hit → paid within 7 days
metrics.definition: Per calendar week of FIRST limit hit: distinct accounts whose first limit impression fell in the week → share with first paid within 7 days of that impression. Count accounts, not modal opens; read only weeks ≥7 days old; pool over 30 days when weekly n < 100.
metrics.benchmark: 15–23% by week, drifting to 11–14% later; 20% of all limit-hitters upgraded (b-limit-hit-paid-within-7-days)
metrics.trap: Modal opens inflate the denominator; a week read before its 7 days close under-reports.

metrics.name: Usage-limit funnel
metrics.definition: Accounts that hit the limit → saw the limit modal (impression event) → clicked its CTA → paid within 24h of the click. Impression and click are separate events with one emitter each. Report each step as a count and as a share of the previous step.
metrics.benchmark: 182 accounts → 42 clicked (23%) → 27 paid within 24h (64% of clicks) (e-06)
metrics.trap: Never mix an impression rate with a click rate; never quote the click→pay rate without n (here 42).

metrics.name: Click → pay within 24h by surface
metrics.definition: For each upgrade surface (limit modal, pre-limit nudge, sidebar, header, email), clicks and first payments within 24h of the click; like for like, clicks vs clicks.
metrics.benchmark: limit modal 64% (27 of 42) · pre-limit 4 of 10 · sidebar 20% · header 10% (e-06, correlation)
metrics.trap: Small n on every surface but the sidebar and header; show counts beside rates.

metrics.name: Time from signup to first paid signal
metrics.definition: For accounts with first paid set (trigger-stamped, never cleared): days between signup and first paid; report median, share on signup day, share within 7 days. Accounts ≥14 days old.
metrics.benchmark: median 0.7 days; ~60% within week one; flat after day 7 (b-when-paying-users-convert)
metrics.trap: Only accounts that ever paid: it says WHEN payers pay, not how many pay. Demote the pitch after day 7 for everyone else.

metrics.name: Paid adds per week
metrics.definition: New first payments per calendar week (first paid stamped by a database trigger, never cleared by cancellation), internal accounts excluded; report a 4-week trend fit.
metrics.benchmark: ~25 a week, flat (R² 0.03 on trend) while the free base grew 54% (e-08)
metrics.trap: The paying total is a stock; steer by adds and the ceiling (adds ÷ monthly churn).

metrics.name: Churn on exposure
metrics.definition: Over the trailing 90 days: subscriptions that ended (explicit cancel, or unpaid past grace) ÷ (paid subscription-days ÷ 30.4), with a Poisson interval; first-paid accounts only; a re-subscribe of a prior payer is not a cancel. Split ended-before-first-renewal vs after.
metrics.benchmark: 13% blended a month (CI 8–20%); 75% of cancels in the first cycle; ~19% past day 30 on 5 cancels (b-churn)
metrics.trap: A start-of-month denominator can report 150%; resubscribers are not churn; below 100 paid account-months show counts and forbid the projection.

metrics.name: Churn-14 by pre-pay active days
metrics.definition: Share of new payers who cancel within 14 days, bucketed by active free days before paying (0–1, 2–3, 4+).
metrics.benchmark: 14.3% at 0–1 days vs 0 of 51 at 4+ (b-churn)
metrics.trap: Post-purchase nudges do not move this; it is decided before the purchase.

metrics.name: Gross lifetime value per payer
metrics.definition: Monthly price ÷ churn_exposure (monthly, blended), quoted with churn's interval as a range; gross of serving and support cost.
metrics.benchmark: ~$69 at $9 and 13% churn (range $45–$112 across the 8–20% interval) (e-14)
metrics.trap: An assumed 7% churn made LTV $129 and every audience look profitable; use the measured interval and never compare a cost per payer to the top of the range.

metrics.name: Email click-then-return
metrics.definition: Per message: delivered recipients who clicked AND made a core request within 24h of the click ÷ delivered recipients. Holdout delta = (share of the sent arm with a core request within 7 days of send) − (same for the 20% control arm recorded as ledger rows at claim time), with an interval.
metrics.benchmark: best message 10 of 436; paid pitches 0 of 274; every holdout flat at 9–13-point detectable effects (e-19, holdout)
metrics.trap: 'Success after send' with no click gating is coincidence (~5× inflated); opens are context only.

metrics.name: Broken-output share
metrics.definition: Share of results persisted incomplete (truncated, severed, errored) per complete reporting-timezone day per surface, with a volume gate (≥250 results); keyed on a field written unconditionally.
metrics.benchmark: 6.1% during a 10-day silent outage; ~2.3% durable after two fixes (e-27)
metrics.trap: An optional flag whose absence is normal reads 0.00% when the flag dies.

metrics.name: Degraded / fallback share
metrics.definition: Share of results served by the fallback path per full day; score complete days only.
metrics.benchmark: 49.8% during a flap; 1.6–1.9% healthy; alert above 20% (e-26)
metrics.trap: Hourly or partial-day reads swung 0.5–56% with no config change. When it is high, set the fallback deadline from the fallback's own latency, well above the primary's p99.

metrics.name: Output-property canary
metrics.definition: Define one output property your product must exhibit when its critical dependency works (an answer cites retrieved data, a payment settles, a map renders). Share of results exhibiting it per hour, against a healthy band set from 14 clean days; instantiate one canary per silently-failing dependency.
metrics.benchmark: 0% for 4 days 5.5 hours at HTTP 200 during a silent outage; the source's healthy band was not recorded
metrics.trap: Monitor the output property, never the dependency's status.

metrics.name: Stream failures within 15 minutes of a deploy
metrics.definition: Per complete day: streamed results that ended without a completion marker and whose start fell within 15 minutes before or after a deploy timestamp ÷ all such incomplete streams that day. Requires a deploy log.
metrics.benchmark: 56% of failures inside the deploy window before streams registered with the shutdown drain (68 streams, 23 deploys, 17 hours) (e-28)
metrics.trap: Without a deploy log the failures look random; a result saved server-side but never delivered still counts as a failure for the user.

metrics.name: Ledger vs processor mismatches
metrics.definition: Nightly: transactions in the processor's export not in your ledger plus ledger rows not at the processor, counted by transaction across both event families (charges and refunds), deduped by fingerprint; report the count even when zero and log the run.
metrics.benchmark: 3 double-charged accounts found by reconcile; 1 had complained
metrics.trap: A silent night is only clean if the job ran.

metrics.name: Ad cost per activated user and per payer
metrics.definition: Per ad, joined to production by campaign tag: spend ÷ signups, ÷ activated users (activated_any_day), ÷ payers; compare cost per payer to gross_ltv.
metrics.benchmark: $5 a signup / ~$37 an activated user / $131 a payer vs ~$69 gross LTV; retargeting $52 (e-14, e-15, e-16)
metrics.trap: Never quote the platform's cost per lead; it overcounted signups by a third and hid a 4× cost rise.

metrics.name: Activated within 7 days (ads threshold)
metrics.definition: Share of signups with ≥N self-initiated core requests on any one reporting-timezone day within 7 days of signup, N = your daily free limit, auto-generated results excluded; denominator: signups joined to the ad by campaign tag.
metrics.benchmark: 11.9% (worst audience) → 31% (best), same ad; 13.4% blended (e-14)
metrics.trap: This is the ads steering threshold, not product activation; never quote it as activation_day0.

metrics.name: Front-door funnel
metrics.definition: Fresh visitors (browser id first seen in the window, bot-filtered, never signed in by staff) → primary action → first own action → signup within 7 days. Every share is of fresh visitors, not of the previous step.
metrics.trap: Instrument before you redesign; there may be no pre-door era to compare against. ≥1,000 fresh visitors per arm before a verdict.

metrics.name: Signups by referrer and AI engine
metrics.definition: Signups per month by first-touch source (ad platform, direct, content pages, each AI answer engine, referral), with the unattributed share decomposed (app installs, platforms that strip parameters).
metrics.benchmark: AI engines ~20 lifetime, 1/3/8/7 by month, rising after the crawler unblock; content pages 35 since tags began; 41% unattributed
metrics.trap: An unattributed bucket that large hides a whole channel; decompose it before concluding anything.

metrics.name: Crawler status per public route
metrics.definition: For every public route and every crawler user agent you care about: HTTP status fetched from outside after a CDN purge; plus the diff between the sitemap and the auth allowlist (must be empty).
metrics.benchmark: every AI crawler 403 for months while robots.txt said allowed; 5 of 11 sitemap routes redirected to login
metrics.trap: robots.txt is not evidence of access.

metrics.name: Element reach × second-day return
metrics.definition: For every UI element: distinct users who saw it (impression) in 90 days × the share of them with a core request on the reporting-timezone day after their FIRST impression; rank by the product.
metrics.benchmark: no absolute score is portable; rank within your product; the bottom of the ranking (a carousel: 9 users in 14 days) was killed
metrics.trap: Click-only instrumentation hides that nobody saw the element; log impressions.

metrics.name: Organic review claims per week
metrics.definition: Reward claims per week with batch-backfill minutes (≥4 grants in one minute) excluded; ask impressions instrumented so the ask has a denominator; click-outs by site.
metrics.benchmark: ~4 a week organic, not the 68 lifetime total; ~3 → ~7 after routing was hedged (e-13)
metrics.trap: Lifetime totals are mostly backfill batches.

metrics.name: Referral yield
metrics.definition: Activated invitees per week (a durable row: the invitee reached activation_day0), with inviter impressions instrumented for a denominator; payouts only on that row.
metrics.benchmark: 1 invitation in two weeks, the team's own test; 13 impressions
metrics.trap: Sends and panel opens are not yield; do not build the loop before intake exists.

metrics.name: Public claims machine-checked
metrics.definition: Share of quoted UI strings, numbers and navigation paths in help and marketing copy checked against code; wrong claims found per audit; copy drift caught by tests pinning identical strings across surfaces.
metrics.benchmark: 643 strings, 90 numbers, 52 paths checked; 12 wrong, 4 telling free users to pay for what they had
metrics.trap: A claim that was true at write time is false the day the product changes.

metrics.name: Critical-path latency
metrics.definition: p50 and p95 per critical call under real load (not solo), time to first byte of the core result, share of long requests cut by the proxy ceiling, payment-form time-to-interactive per day.
metrics.benchmark: answer 15.3s → 2.4s; first byte 5–7s → 0.5–0.7s; a dashboard query 40.8s → 1.03s solo but 3.4s under load (e-22, e-25)
metrics.trap: Solo timings lie; the burst is the failure.

metrics.name: Support ticket mix
metrics.definition: Hand-labelled sample of ≥100 tickets per month (or every ticket below that volume), labelled before any routing rule sees them: product use attempted through the support box, grounded how-to, real bug, needs a human.
metrics.benchmark: ~20% / ~40% / ~15% / rest (b-support-mix)
metrics.trap: Keyword-classifying to decide autonomy put a churn threat in the how-to bucket.

metrics.name: Ticket to verified fix
metrics.definition: Hours from ticket to a fix merged, serving and verified against that report; drafts older than 48 hours with no human decision, counted daily.
metrics.benchmark: five users waited 62–95 hours behind an empty-looking queue; one held draft retried 5,749 times
metrics.trap: A rule that quietly removes tickets from the queue is worse than no rule.

metrics.name: Differentiator adoption
metrics.definition: Accounts using the headline capability, counted by a durable row (a subscription, a completed migration), never a page view; per week.
metrics.benchmark: 4 rows and 0 published sites weeks after launch while a look-alike table read as adoption
metrics.trap: Count the right table; a page view is not adoption.

metrics.name: Preference honor rate
metrics.definition: Share of user-set preferences honored on output, measured by replaying real inputs through the current system; anything that must be reliable is code.
metrics.benchmark: a formatting preference ignored in ~1 of 3 outputs until enforced in code; 45 of 74 real outputs corrected, 0 collateral (e-31)
metrics.trap: Asking a probabilistic component more firmly is the fix that has already been tried twice.

metrics.name: Audit yield
metrics.definition: Confirmed defects per adversarial review pass, and reversals (published claims later retracted) per month.
metrics.benchmark: 7–36 confirmed defects per pass; fixes reintroduced defects in 3 of 4 rounds (b-audit-yield)
metrics.trap: Zero reversals means the audit is confirming, not auditing.

journey.name: Before users: build the instruments
journey.goal: Ship the ledger, the one sentence, the one price and the daily canary before there is any traffic to measure.
you_are_here_when: Zero to a handful of accounts, none of them measured.
No event ledger, or one with no impression events.
No published free limit or paid price yet.
journey.feels_like: You have a product that works for you and you cannot say what a user did yesterday without reading a database by hand.

do_now.move: Log every page view and click with a stable anonymous id before signup; fire conversion events on completed behavior, not clicks.
Write one internal-account rule and apply it in every counter; drop bots at ingestion; clamp client clocks.
Record the system's own decisions on the result row (which path served it, degraded or not, which variant) so failures are a query.
Write the one-sentence value proposition; if it needs a second sentence, positioning is not done.
One paid plan that removes a published usage ceiling; no trial; a free tier that is genuinely useful under the limit.
Design the first session to end in a real result before any preference question.
Write the daily read-only health check now, keyed on a field written unconditionally; it reports every day, quiet or not.
Decide the definitions once: active = a core request; timezone named; day zero is the denominator; today dropped.

readiness.threshold: Every convertible surface has an impression event and every money event has exactly one emitter
readiness.note: Reset your reporting epoch to the minute this is true.

journey.name: First traffic: get the first 200 users and read every downvote
journey.goal: Buy or earn a small, measured stream of visitors, let them use the product before signing up, and fix the top cause of every negative signal within days.
you_are_here_when: A first paid campaign, post or listing is live or about to be.
Negative ratings and abandoned sessions exist and nobody has read them this week.
journey.feels_like: Real traffic has started and you can name your users but not yet your funnel.

do_now.move: Buy a small fixed weekly budget on one audience, ad written as the concrete task, joined to production by campaign tag from day one; treat it as a usage buy, not a payer buy.
Verify every public route is fetchable from outside with each crawler's own user agent before the first post or listing.
Let visitors use the product before they sign up; gate the save, not the value.
Screenshot every front door at phone width on a production build; expect most signups on a phone (74% here).
Every 3–5 days: read every negative rating and transcript; fix the top cause; write the hand-off.
Zero interruptions: no tour on first load, no auto-starting guide, no modal between the user and the thing they were doing.
One primary action on the front door, and it is the product itself.

readiness.threshold: ≥70% of requesters make their first request within 1 hour
<30% of setup completers with zero requests, among accounts ≥7 days old
readiness.note: Reference 38% on a snapshot that still included same-day signups; expect lower under the recipe.

journey.name: Activation: the first hour, then the first week
journey.goal: Turn a first session into a first week: a result before any question, depth on day zero, a return on day one, and a scoreboard that cannot flatter you.
you_are_here_when: At least one closed 7-day cohort of ≥100 signups (the retention curve is readable).
Setup completion is high and a large share of completers make no request.
journey.feels_like: Hundreds to low thousands of users; the weekly numbers move and you are not sure why.

do_now.move: Generate the first result before asking; make every completion moment do something with what was just completed.
Delete every setup field under 20% fill; move style, tone and format questions to after the first result.
One setup flow every surface derives from; one suggestion system; suggestions from what people organically do first.
Monday scoreboard with dated four- and ten-week targets: day-zero depth, week-one return, engaged weekly actives, per tenure.
Kill anything with ≥50 exposures and 0 successes; ship dark behind a flag so a decision day is a config flip.
Record 20% holdouts for anything you claim moves return.

readiness.threshold: ≥8% day-zero activation (3+ requests and a saved result)
Week-one return ≥30% under the request definition on a closed cohort of ≥100
readiness.note: Diagnostic beside it: expect a monotonic depth spread (14% → 56% here); if depth rises and the cohort rate does not, the depth was manufactured.

readiness.threshold: Week-2 engagement ≥20% and level, not falling

journey.name: Monetize: the limit is the pitch
journey.goal: Walk activated users to a hard usage limit on real value, make the first hit a clean single-CTA pitch, publish the limit and never test it per customer, and record every money fact when it happens.
you_are_here_when: ≥10 accounts hit the free limit per day for 7 days.
A paid plan exists and first payments are stamped by a trigger.
journey.feels_like: Users reach the free limit every day and you are tempted by a trial, a second plan or a discount anchor.

do_now.move: First limit hit: one CTA, show what they would lose, nothing to scroll; escape offers only from hit-day two.
Publish the limit everywhere and never A/B it per customer; annual is a switch on the same plan, not a second package.
Paywall at send after they have built the thing, never on a cold click; pitch inside week one and demote after day seven.
Charge before creating the subscription; one checkout in flight per account; cancel never disabled or gated on an essay.
Judge any price or plan change by paid adds per week over ≥4 weeks against the pre-change rate, never by the paying total or daily actives.
Separate impression and click events for every offer surface, one emitter each; stamp first paid by a database trigger.
Social proof live and exact: user count, real feedback curated in the database, listing ratings on a cache.
Ask for reviews in-app after value, on day one or later with real usage, never by email; same reward for everyone asked.
Measure churn on exposure and by pre-pay tenure from the first cohort that faces renewal.

readiness.threshold: ≥15% of limit-hitting accounts pay within 7 days, pooled over 30 days
readiness.note: Reference 15–23% by week. Diagnostic: limit-modal click → pay ≥50% on ≥100 clicks and impression → click ≥20%.

readiness.threshold: Churn on exposure computed on ≥100 paid account-months with an interval, first-cycle split from post-renewal; below that show counts and forbid the projection

journey.name: Retain and return
journey.goal: Bring users back with their own unfinished work, prove every retention claim with a holdout, cut what returns nobody, and add referrals only once intake exists.
you_are_here_when: ≥1 lifecycle message live with no holdout row in the ledger.
Opens above 30% and no message with a measured return.
journey.feels_like: Opens look healthy and you cannot say what they caused.

do_now.move: Behavior-triggered engine with a claim-before-send ledger; global caps; every email deep-links to a specific object.
Record 20% holdouts as ledger rows; judge every message by click-then-return and holdout delta; never pitch money by email.
Keep the product name out of subject lines; a question or the recipient's own context wins.
Push: one primer card, then the OS dialog only at a value moment; count reach as id + opted-in + token.
Biweekly: rank every element by reach × second-day return; cut the tail; never regrow without a holdout.
Trace one churned user second by second before theorizing; read frustration from repeat clicks and typed retries.
Read what users believe the product is: typed intents vs your examples, return timing, which surface converts, what they file as support.
Referral rewards pay on a qualified durable row (the invitee activates), never on send; the ask sits in-app after a value moment; do not build the loop before intake exists.

readiness.threshold: Every live message shows click-then-return ≥1% on ≥100 recipients AND its 20% holdout delta is not negative at the detectable effect size; a flat-holdout message stays only if it announces a product state; everything else cut
readiness.note: Reference: every holdout flat; 'your allowance is back' returned 66%.

readiness.threshold: ≥90% of tickets carry a lane (product-use-through-support / grounded how-to / real bug / needs a human) before any reply
readiness.note: Reference: ~20% were product use attempted through the support box.

journey.name: Acquire: ads, doors and proof
journey.goal: Buy and earn intake only where cost per activated user clears lifetime value, verify every path from ad to destination as a real user, and treat every front door as an experiment.
you_are_here_when: limit_hit_to_paid_7d rising over 4 weeks while signups per week are flat within ±10%.
A campaign budget exists or is about to.
journey.feels_like: Conversion is improving and intake is flat; the lever is intake.

do_now.move: Join every ad to production by campaign tag; steer on cost per activated user and per payer vs gross LTV; never the platform's CPL.
Rank audiences before creatives; hold creative constant across audiences; scale by spend rate per audience.
Put the pixel on every page a campaign points at and never on pages you host for customers; verify it fires as a real user before spend.
Fund top-of-funnel as a usage buy only while cost per activated user is tracked; fund retargeting only where cost per payer clears LTV.
Write the ad as the concrete task; verify the ad's landing → signup → destination path as a real user before spending.
Treat any front-door change as an A/B with signups per fresh visitor within 7 days as the metric.
Public page = route + auth allowlist; root domain never redirects; structured data asserts only sourceable facts; measure yield by referrer or say unmeasured.
Research before building: a graded competitor matrix, public complaints, and the one capability incumbents cannot copy.

readiness.threshold: Cost per payer below gross LTV (measured interval) for every audience you keep
readiness.note: Reference $131 vs ~$69 top-of-funnel was LTV-negative; retargeting $52 cleared.

readiness.threshold: Signups per fresh visitor within 7 days ≥ the pre-change arm on ≥1,000 fresh visitors per arm; a redesign that does not move it is reverted or kept on cost, not on the leak
readiness.note: Reference 12.9%; the primary-action rate held at 24–28% across four redesigns.

journey.name: Scale and predict
journey.goal: Model the business as a line, run reliability like a growth channel, make support a bug pipeline, keep the audit cadence as the operating system, and add a second product only when the first is forecastable.
you_are_here_when: paid_adds_per_week ≥ 20 for 4 consecutive weeks AND churn_exposure has an interval.
Deploys more than once a day and at least one silent failure found by audit rather than by ticket.
journey.feels_like: Thousands of users, a paying base, and a forecast someone believes.

do_now.move: Model the base as intake × retention plateau; quote the ceiling (adds ÷ churn) and weekly adds; backtest every projection on a dated schedule.
Daily canaries on output properties; report every day including quiet days.
Fallback deadlines from the fallback's own latency, well above the primary's p99; trip on two stalls.
Every stream registered with the deploy drain; deploys batched.
Aggregate in the database; gate heavy reads; never cache a degraded read.
Fail closed where a wrong yes costs money or data; fail open where a read blip would lock out payers; write both down.
Every ticket, form and thumbs-down becomes a job; fix, hostile second read, verify against the report, then reply.
Deny-by-default sends with a database-row kill switch; classify tickets before routing.
Adversarial review with an independent refuter per finding on every money change and large change; fewer than two verdicts is unreviewed.
Make anything the customer must rely on deterministic code, with probabilistic components as fallback; shadow-test any vendor or algorithm swap.
A second product or major new surface only after paid adds and churn are forecastable; run the graded competitor matrix and public-complaint read first, time-boxed to a multiple of build time.
Count adoption of any new surface by a durable row (subscription, completed migration), never a page view; no doors from the first product into it until its own funnel is instrumented.
Config-flip kill switches for every launch; a kill switch is a rollback, never a hide.

audits.cadence: weekly if an agent works the queue

readiness.threshold: <2.5% on every complete day, reported daily including quiet days
Last month's projection landed within ±20% of actual paid adds; the ceiling is quoted as adds ÷ monthly churn with churn's interval
readiness.note: Reference ~25 ÷ 0.13 ≈ 190 paying accounts at the ceiling, interval ~125–310.

readiness.threshold: Nightly reconcile ran and reported a count (zero or not) every night this month
readiness.note: Reference: 3 double charges found by reconcile, 1 complained.
